Riley Morgan: Quick Q - rented a van for a 3-city roadshow. We had one company card decline at the fuel pump so one person paid cash for fuel and tolls across multiple legs. How should we submit these split receipts?
Maria (People Ops): Short answer: submit a single expense per person with clear allocation notes.
Riley Morgan: We have one big paper toll ticket (consecutive tolls on one slip) and multiple fuel receipts in cash and cc. Can we aggregate?
Sam Patel (Finance): You can aggregate per day/driver but must show itemized proof. For tolls: upload the full toll slip and annotate who was on which leg. For cash fuel: attach receipts and a brief mileage log showing miles driven per leg.
Oliver (Ops): We assigned drivers A/B/C across legs. Should I create separate claims for each driver or one pooled claim allocating to drivers?
Maria (People Ops): Best practice: each claimant submits their own claim for expenses they paid. If one person paid cash on behalf of the team, that person submits the expense and in the description list the beneficiaries and cost splits. Include manager approval confirming cost allocation.
Sam Patel (Finance): For coding in Expensely (copy/paste):
```
Expense type: "Ground Transportation - Rental & Tolls"
Project/Cost center: "Events - Roadshow Q2"
GL account: "5110 - Ground Transportation"
Description: "Van rental, fuel and tolls split across team. Payer: Riley Morgan (cash). Allocation: Riley 40%, Oliver 30%, Maya 30%. Manager approval attached. Mileage log included."
Required attachments: rental_agreement.pdf, toll_slip.pdf, fuel_receipts_1-4.pdf, proof_of_payment_cash.jpg, mileage_log.pdf, manager_approval.pdf
```
Sam Patel (Finance): If you're doing internal allocation, include a short CSV or note mapping amounts to cost centers if different teams are splitting. If refunds between teammates are needed, finance does not process peer-to-peer reimbursements; handle those outside Expensely and only claim what the company owes the payer.
Riley Morgan: Got it. One more: the rental agency charged a refueling fee because we returned the van with 1/4 tank. We filled up afterwards; can we claim the refuel receipt instead of the agency fee?
Maria (People Ops): If you have a fuel receipt showing you refueled after return, we can reimburse the actual fuel cost instead of the agency fee, but attach both the rental agency invoice showing the refuel charge and your fuel receipt for comparison. Finance will net the cheaper option per policy.
expense-bot: Reminder: redact license plate/personal ID on receipts. Max 10MB per attachment.
Riley Morgan: Thanks — I'll prepare individual claims and manager note now.
